correctness.rationale: The exact Poisson age mixture, Gaussian conditional variance, bounded-drift estimates and age tail controls establish the leading rate. The first √R correction is proved by a sharp drift upper bound, positive Brownian angular tube probabilities for every fixed D_r>0, and a deterministic-heading Laplace expansion when D_r=0. A unique monotone saddle and the envelope theorem prove all rate inequalities. Finite checker tests corroborate rather than establish these results.

value.rationale: The high-reset stationary mean-square displacement collapses as r^-3, while rare √r-scale excursions select old reset ages. The theorem distinguishes a universal leading thermal rate from a subleading, singular orientational-memory effect: any positive rotational diffusivity isotropizes rare tails at order √R, while frozen headings retain anisotropy. This supplies meaningful angular tail diagnostics not available from finite moments or the known passive saddle.
